$comment: tag: flock = stated in a Flock document; independent = documented by an independent source; both = stated by Flock and documented independently; unknown = not published by Flock and not verified by an independent source.

hops.title: Capture
hops.summary: The passive infrared sensor triggers on a warm moving object. The camera captures six to 12 still frames of the vehicle's rear, illuminated at night by an 850 nm infrared array.
unknowns: People and cyclists that trigger the sensor appear in frame; Flock states they are not indexed

hops.title: On-device inference
hops.summary: The plate and its state are read with a confidence score, and the vehicle is described in what Flock calls a “Vehicle Fingerprint.” Flock's policy says the plate and vehicle images are transferred to its cloud.

hops.title: Metadata
hops.summary: Timestamp, GPS position from the patch antenna and the device identifier are attached.
unknowns: Direction of travel as an indexed field is not confirmed in any public source

hops.title: Uplink over LTE
hops.transport: HTTPS and TLS, according to Flock, over a carrier SIM
hops.summary: Each read is transmitted over the cellular module. In December 2025 and January 2026, researchers found dozens of Flock devices, most of them Condor video cameras, reachable on public cellular addresses with an administration page that needed no password; one researcher said some plate readers were among them. Flock said only Condor cameras were affected and cited carrier testing.
unknowns: How the camera proves its identity to the cloud
How many reads a standard Falcon holds while offline

hops.title: Arrival
hops.summary: Flock's architecture summary says the data is encrypted with Amazon's key management service before it is sent, and checked when it arrives.

hops.title: Indexing
hops.summary: Software services index the read so it can be searched and send out alerts through Amazon's notification service; separate tools produce aggregate statistics, Flock's architecture summary says.
payload: an alert, if the plate matched

hops.title: Storage
hops.storage: Images in object storage (S3), records in databases (RDS and DynamoDB), encrypted at rest, according to Flock
hops.summary: Flock's policy says plate reads are transferred to Amazon's government cloud, and a company post says all data covered by the F.B.I.'s criminal-justice information rules is stored there.
unknowns: Independent confirmation of where the plate reads are stored
A FIPS 140 certificate for Flock's modules is referenced by Flock but not publicly listed

hops.title: Hot list match
hops.summary: The plate is compared with hot lists: the F.B.I.'s National Crime Information Center and the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children, Flock's policy says, and Amber Alerts and custom lists that agencies write themselves, according to its datasheet. The A.C.L.U. found that the cameras download the F.B.I.'s NCIC list only twice a day, so a plate removed from it can keep producing alerts for up to 12 hours.

hops.title: Alert
hops.transport: A push notification; the app sends alerts to officers within a set radius
hops.summary: When a plate matches, an alert with the time, the camera's location, the plate and the vehicle image reaches officers in 10 to 15 seconds on average, according to Flock's datasheet; Flock's mobile app sends alerts to officers within a set radius. Multi-factor login became mandatory in August 2026. In Roseville, Calif., 1,011 of 1,427 stolen-vehicle and felony alerts in 2023 and 2024 (71 percent) involved a misread plate; the department says none led to a contact or an arrest, and Flock calls the figure a mischaracterization of overall accuracy.

hops.title: Network search
hops.summary: A user in a customer agency can search by plate, description, natural language or co-traveling vehicles, across the agency's cameras, its sharing partners, and the national lookup that about 75 percent of law enforcement customers joined, according to Flock's statement to Congress. The audit log of a Johnson County, Tex., search on May 9, 2025, lists 83,345 cameras in 6,809 networks.
unknowns: Whether derived metadata is deleted on the same clock as images

hops.title: Audit log
hops.summary: Each search writes a row. Exports released under public records requests show the fields. Other agencies' searches of an agency's cameras appear with the operator and plate redacted. EFF found about one in five reasons across 12 million searches were generic terms such as “investigation”; ALPRWatch documented rows changing after the fact.

hops.title: Delete
hops.retention: Seven days by default for new customers since Aug. 13, 2026, down from 30; existing customers keep the periods they set; longer where an elected body approved it; Evidence Mode keeps data tied to an investigation, with no published limit
hops.summary: According to Flock, an automated Amazon Web Services S3 lifecycle policy deletes images once they pass the agency’s retention period, and AWS CloudTrail logs each deletion. As of Oct. 8, 2026, Flock's Myths and Facts page still gives 30 days as the default; its Data Privacy page gives seven.

deputy.reasonAsLogged: had an abortion, search for female
deputy.caseNumber: the case number of the sheriff's office death investigation

accounts.who: Johnson County Sheriff Adam King, to 404 Media
accounts.text: Her family was worried that she was going to bleed to death, and we were trying to find her to get her to a hospital.
She was being searched for as a missing person, not as a suspect of a crime.

accounts.who: EFF, from the incident report and the lead detective's affidavit
accounts.text: The records describe a death investigation of a nonviable fetus; the abortion took place more than two weeks before deputies were called.

deputy.note: Reproduced from the audit logs of two searches by the Johnson County, Tex., sheriff's office on May 9, 2025, reported by 404 Media and documented by EFF: one week across 17,684 cameras in 1,295 networks, then a month across 83,345 cameras in 6,809 networks. Both logged the same reason and the case number of the office's death investigation.
